To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thiram was most effective in inducing TD in chickens.
a short feeding period of thiram during the 1st 2 wk of life was sufficient to produce TD in a high percentage (>50%) of birds.
the dithiocarbates induce tibial cartilage lesions in poultry and that the lesions appear to be caused by the inhibition of the chondroblast proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an animal model to study the pathogenesis of TD in chickens.
the identification of micronutrients and their mechanisms of actions in preventing or ameliorating TD in poultry.
the development of a new animal model of metabolic cartilage disease and its use for the study of pathogenesis and prevention of the naturally occurring condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thiram is the most efficient dithiocarbamic compound to induce TD in young chickens.
thiram was the most potent of 3 dithio- carbamates tested to induce TD and that a short exposure to thiram during the early stages of life was sufficient to induce severe lesions of the disease.
the thiram feeding method is a useful tool in studying TD in chickens and the results of the study will provide a useful basis for future research on this disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TD is induced by thiram and the effect is long-lasting.
thiram is a useful agent to induce tibiotarsal dyschondroplaia in chickens and that the effects of thiram can be seen within the first 2 d of its administration.

the dithiocarbamide thiram, a potent inducer of tibial dyscondroplasia in young chickens, can be used as a model system to study the pathogenesis of this disease and to identify protective micronutrients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a short-term exposure of chickens to thiram during the early posthatch period can induce TD and that the induced lesions are long-lasting and can be used to study the pathogenesis of TD.
thiram, a dithiocarbamic pesticide, can induce TD and that this induction is not associated with any significant change in serum concentrations of Ca and P, 2 major components of bone matrix.
the experimental protocol to induce and study TD can be accomplished in a short time period of 3 to 5 wk.
